title: Cohomological and Tor bounds on comparison pullback of etale closed-support values
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-sf-categories], the comparison morphisms $\nu_S:S_{\mathrm{proet}}\to S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and intrinsically bounded constructible pro-etale complexes [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow T$. Assume the ordinary etale open-complement condition at $A$ with constant $c\geq0$ [def-exc-open-complement-bound]: $R^qj_*M=0$ for every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ on $W$ and $q>c$, and $R^qj_*$ preserves constructible sheaves for every $q$. Let $i_e^!$ be the ambient ordinary etale right adjoint to closed direct image [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. For $K_e\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put $C_e=i_e^!K_e$ and $C_p=\nu_Z^*C_e$. For all integers $r\leq s$ the following two implications hold independently.

(a) If $K_e$ has cohomology only in $[r,s]$, then $C_e\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $C_p\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals]. No finite-Tor hypothesis is required.

(b) If $K_e$ has etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], then $C_e$ is bounded constructible with etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s+c+1]$, and $C_p$ is intrinsically bounded constructible with pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[r,s+c+1]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. In particular, for every degree-zero pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $N$ on $Z$, with no etale-origin restriction,
$$\mathcal H^t(C_p\otimes_A^LN)=0\quad(t\notin[r,s+c+1]).$$

proof.text: For (a), apply [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] with $(T,Z,i,j,A,a,b,c)=(T,Z,i,j,A,r,s,c)$. Its vanishing hypothesis is exactly the first part of the assumed open-complement condition, and its constructibility hypothesis is exactly the second part. The coefficient ring is finite, $c\geq0$, $K_e$ is bounded constructible, and its stipulated cohomological interval is $[r,s]$. The constructible clause of that lemma therefore gives $C_e=i_e^!K_e\in D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. This application uses no Tor assumption. In Lean, first transport both clauses of the open-complement condition from the bounded-below derived direct image to the unbounded one using Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Package the resulting interval and constructible cohomology as isBoundedConstructible.

source.place: Both paragraphs: ordinary etale amplitude and the additional constructibility clause.

proof.text: Apply the forward essential-image clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin] to the identity witness of the bounded constructible object C_e from Step 1. It supplies intrinsically constructible cohomology and a finite vanishing interval for the specified finiteCoefficientIntrinsicDerivedComparison. The nonzero cohomology support is contained in that finite integer interval, so it is finite. Exactness of the canonical comparison preserves homologyConcentratedIn [r,s+c+1] by the generic exact-functor t-structure lemma. Degreewise vanishing then puts its support in the same inclusive interval. This is [def-weil-constructible-intervals], completing (a).

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; exact inverse image and cohomology compatibility: sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), as stated by lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact.

proof.text: For (b), start independently with the Tor hypothesis on the bounded constructible K_e. Reuse the generic closed_support_boundedConstructible_torAmplitude proof of [prop-exc-closed-tor], with the constant residue module of the lifted coefficient ring. To instantiate its residue test [lem-exc-residue-tor-test], let r_0 be the image of the recorded uniformizer in A. The DVR statement [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] for the data of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] makes (r_0) maximal, and r_0^n=0 by the definition of the quotient and n>=1. The ring equivalence A ≃ ULift A maps this principal ideal to (ULift.up r_0), preserving maximality and nilpotence. The generic residue_test proof therefore applies literally to the universe-lifted ring. Its quotient residue module is finite as a quotient of a finite ring. The same open-complement hypotheses transported in Step 1 give bounded constructibility of C_e and Tor amplitude [r,s+c+1]. No cohomological premise of (a) is used.

source.place: Closed-support Tor bound, applied with input interval [r,s].

proof.text: The bounded constructible C_e from Step 3 belongs to D^+. Apply the forward implication of [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] with interval [r,s+c+1], which is ordered since c>=0. Its stated comparison is intrinsic realization after the bounded-below fixed-scalar inverse image. Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility identify this object with the specified unbounded intrinsic comparison of C_e. For each K-flat representative, compose its representing isomorphism with this identification and apply the Tor test. This retains the quantification over every degree-zero pro-etale module sheaf, without an etale-origin restriction, as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Independently repeat the forward essential-image argument of Step 2 for intrinsic bounded constructibility. This completes (b).

source.place: Forward implication: bounded flat model pulled back termwise and tensored with an arbitrary pro-etale module sheaf; constructibility is Tag 09AL, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-constructible-derived.

proof_origin.place: H4, 2026-10-24: Lean proof following the same closed-support amplitude/residue/comparison route, with the canonical finite-ring intrinsic constructible comparison to avoid converting the continuous-coefficient origin presentation. Reuse the generic proved helpers of prop-exc-closed-tor and lem-exc-residue-tor-test for the coefficient ULift; explicit plus/unbounded and composite-comparison isomorphisms supply the interface glue.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-1ba88fb32 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full; there are no new nodes. Step 1: lem-exc-closed-amplitude with (a,b)=(r,s). A=O_E/ϖ^n is finite, and the two clauses of def-exc-open-complement-bound are exactly the lemma's vanishing and constructibility hypotheses. This gives i_e^!K_e in étale D_c^{[r,s+c+1]}; the étale interval notation is defined in def-sf-categories. Step 2: clause (ii) of lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin (Stacks 09AL, proetale.tex l.5357) gives intrinsic D^b_c(Z,A), which is the same category as def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility. Clause (3) of lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact (Stacks 04JC) keeps the interval. Step 3: prop-exc-closed-tor matches literally (A=O_E/ϖ^n, quasi-compact j, same def-kun-tor-amplitude) and does not use the premise of (a). Step 4: the forward direction of lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval applies to C_e, which is bounded and so in D^+. Its conclusion is def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, tested against every pro-étale N. Edge cases checked: Z empty, i=id, and 0 in A^1 with c=1, where i^!A=A(-1)[-2] lies in [0,2]. At n>1, (a) and (b) are correctly kept independent. Accepted tool_uses: lem-exc-closed-amplitude and prop-exc-closed-tor are named in the main-20261015 thm-pur-general-admissibility proof Step 2; lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval is a generic site-comparison tool.
